newsitem.title: THAILAND: Opposition grill Thai ministers on budget.
newsitem.headline: Opposition grill Thai ministers on budget.

text.p: Thai opposition parties on Friday stepped up their attack on the government's proposed austerity budget for fiscal 1998, accusing ministers of reneging on promises.
Education minister Sukavit Rangsitphol, who was allocated a hefty increase in spending, bore the brunt of criticism for the third and final day of the budget debate in Parliament.
"His big budget isn't meant to reform education but rather on reforming a new channel to make money," said Somsak Prisnanunthakul, from the opposition Chart Thai. Sukavit rejected the allegations.
Members of the 393-seat lower house will vote on the budget bill late on Friday or early Saturday. It was expected to pass easily because of the government's comfortable majority.

Education spending is set to rise by more than five percent to 166.31 billion baht ($6.4 billion) in the next fiscal year (October/September). This was the second-highest allocation after the interior ministry.
Overall, the austerity budget lifts spending by a modest four percent to 982 billion baht, as the government struggles to balance its books in face of Thailand's chronic economic crisis.
The country is expected to post a hefty budget deficit of more than 60 billion baht in fiscal 1997, its first shortfall in a decade.
Earlier, opposition parties had accused the minister for overspending on plans to buy computers for small rural schools.

Transport and Communications Minister Suwat Liptapallop also came under heavy attack for heavy cuts in planned spending on projects linked to seaports in southern Thailand. "The government slashed to 265 million baht from 2.985 billion baht a total set earlier for the construction of a highway in the south. This shows how sincere the government is towards the people," said Manoj Pichaikul of the opposition Democrat Party.
The government has pledged a balanced, deficit-free budget in fiscal 1997/98 but says it needs to ask state enterprises to contribute an additional 16.34 billion baht.

The opposition has predicted both this year's budget and next year's will be hit by deficits because of shortfalls in tax revenue triggered by the economic downturn, the worst in more than a decade. ($ = 25.85 Thai Baht)
